implementation_constraints: reads one JSON value from stdin, prints one line, exits 0

unresolved_intent.decision: Applied the deadline sweep only to jobs already in the ready set (which by construction includes the job that ran last tick), not to jobs still pending arrival
unresolved_intent.rationale: The spec says 'every ready or running job whose deadline is <= the current tick'; a not-yet-arrived job is neither ready nor running, so a job with deadline <= arrival is never dropped before it arrives — it arrives at its tick and is then missed at that same tick by step 2 of that tick.

unresolved_intent.decision: When the job that ran last tick is removed by the deadline sweep, last_run_id is cleared and no preempt event is emitted for it; the newly picked job emits start/resume normally
unresolved_intent.rationale: The spec conditions preempt on 'last tick's job is still ready'. A job dropped at step 2 is no longer ready at selection time, so preempt would contradict the stated condition.

unresolved_intent.decision: Execution decrements remaining then tests remaining <= 0, so a duration-0 job emits start and complete at the same tick and the tick still advances by one
unresolved_intent.rationale: AC-SC-05 mandates start+complete at the same tick. Decrement-then-test makes remaining go to -1 for duration 0; the <= 0 test (rather than == 0) keeps that case on the completion path without a separate branch.

unresolved_intent.decision: On an idle tick last_run_id is reset to None, so a job that was preempted (or was running) before an idle gap emits resume — never a second start — when picked again, and no spurious preempt is emitted after the gap
unresolved_intent.rationale: An idle tick means nothing was ready, so no job 'ran last tick'; the started flag is per-job and survives independently, which preserves INV-SC-PROGRESS-01 (remaining duration is never reset) while keeping the start/resume distinction correct.

unresolved_intent.decision: json.loads failures and all contract violations are funneled through one except (ValueError, MalformedInput) branch that prints ERROR and returns exit code 0
unresolved_intent.rationale: The spec requires exit 0 and the exact token ERROR on any malformed input; ValueError covers JSONDecodeError on Python 3.8+, and a dedicated exception type keeps validation failures distinct from genuine bugs in the simulation, which are left to surface as a crash rather than being masked as ERROR.
